pr_body:
Closes #70219.

Introduce a declarative way for the Elasticsearch server to manage plugins, which reads the `elasticsearch-plugins.yml` file and works which plugins need to be added and / or removed to match the configuration. Also make it possible to configure a proxy in the config file, instead of through the environment.

Most of the work of adding and removing is still done in the `InstallPluginAction` and `RemovePluginAction` classes, so the behaviour should be the same as with the `install` and `remove` commands. However, these commands will now abort if the above config file exists. The intent is to make it harder for the configuration to drift.

This new method only applies to `docker` distribution types at the moment.

Since this syncing mechanism declarative, rather than imperative, the Cloud-specific plugin wrapper script is no longer required. Instead, an environment variable informs `InstallPluginAction` to install plugins from an archive directory instead of downloading them, where possible.
pr_comment:
To summarize what we discussed in our sync:

1. We'll go ahead and implement this only for the Docker packaging type.
2. We'll also publicly document this feature, but again, with the caveat that it's only usable by Docker deployments.
3. We'll ditch the `sync` command in favor for moving this code into node bootstrap.
4. We'll fail to start if we see an `elasticsearch-plugins.yml` file and we are _not_ running via Docker.

@mark-vieira @rjernst can you please take a look at what I've done in `Bootstrap` before I take this any further?

In particular, I had to do some jiggery-pokery in `distribution/build.gradle` so that the BouncyCastle jars aren't generally available outside the ES at runtime, because the security CLI uses different BC jars, and you can't have different BC impls in the same classpath. Open to better ideas here. We use BC during plugin installation for verifying GPG signatures.

In fact moving the jars while building the distribution isn't sufficient, because the `thirdPartyAudit` tasks for `identity-provider` and `security` still fail. I wonder if some stronger kind of isolation is needed - loading the BC jars in their own classloader during bootstrap or something like that.

We can't include bouncy castle on the main classpath. I think we will need to construct a separate classloader to load the plugin-cli classes. We shouldn't need to do any magic there, the bouncy castle jars already exist under `lib/tools/plugin-cli`. How we interact with the classloader is up for debate. One way would be to create an SPI interface in server, which is implemented in plugin-cli. Alternatively we could just grab the necessary action classes through reflection.

I've reworked these changes as follows:

   * Almost all the code is under `distribution/tools/plugin-cli`
   * Bootstrap calls into a small `PluginsManager` class, which creates a class loader and executes a sync action (not a command)
   * When Elasticsearch run the sync action, it creates a `LoggerTerminal` and passes that to the action. I did experiment with just using `Terminal.DEFAULT`, but that just writes to the console. In a Docker container, that results in a mix of JSON and plain text.
   * I also added `Terminal#isHeadless()`, so that the CLI-centric log messages can be tailored to look less weird in the ES log

I also raised #78552 to carve out the Docker improvements that I made during the course of this PR.

I expect to need more testing, but what is here ought to more-or-less work.
@mark-vieira back to you for another review please.

@mark-vieira I've added support for testing plugin installation on all Docker flavours, using the `analysis-icu` plugin. Can you check what I did with the task / configuration / artifact wiring, please?

I also tried to re-enable `PluginCliTests`, which I believe you last disabled, but something isn't working and I disabled them again.
I talked to Cloud Delivery and it doesn't look like the wrapper script is being used, so we're good to merge.
Oh, and I will add docs but I think that'll require some collaboration with the Docs folks, so I'll do that separately.
I think we missed backporting this to 8.0 although we did to 7.16.

review_comment: Is the only reason we are not allowing this for other distributions because we don't yet have packaging tests for it outside of docker?
We're limiting this to Docker because of the rabbit hole around distribution file permissions we run into for archive and package distributions we discovered when discussing this a few weeks back.
